abstract: In this paper, we explore the design and capabilities of GPT-style autoregressive language models, focusing on their generative potential and the underlying scaling laws that govern their performance. We propose a refined architecture that incorporates novel attention mechanisms and improved training strategies, aimed at enhancing in-context learning and emergent abilities. Through extensive experiments on diverse datasets such as WikiText-103 and OpenAI's WebGPT, we demonstrate that our model not only achieves state-of-the-art results in text generation tasks but also exhibits superior performance in few-shot learning scenarios. Our findings reveal that careful consideration of model depth and width, combined with strategic training approaches, can significantly improve the generative capabilities of large language models. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the dynamics of autoregressive LLMs and sets the stage for future innovations in the field.

researchContributions.description: We introduce a transformer architecture with 48 layers and a hidden dimension of 4096, utilizing multi-query attention to reduce computational overhead while maintaining performance.
researchContributions.novelty: This architecture achieves a balance between depth and efficiency, allowing for more scalable implementations of LLMs.

researchContributions.description: We implement a hybrid training strategy that combines curriculum learning with dynamic learning rate adjustments, optimizing the model's learning trajectory.
researchContributions.novelty: This method enables the model to grasp complex patterns earlier in training, leading to improved generative capabilities.

researchContributions.description: By incorporating context-aware attention mechanisms, our model shows a marked improvement in few-shot learning tasks, significantly outperforming previous models.
researchContributions.novelty: This approach allows the model to leverage examples more effectively, demonstrating a better understanding of context across various prompts.

methodology.approach: We adopt a transformer-based autoregressive model with a focus on optimizing both the architecture and training methodologies to enhance generative capabilities.
methodology.modelArchitecture: The model consists of 48 transformer layers, each with a hidden size of 4096 and an attention head count of 32, employing multi-query attention to optimize the attention computation.
methodology.trainingStrategy: The model is trained on a large corpus of 300GB of text data using a mixed-precision training approach, with a batch size of 2048 and a learning rate schedule that starts at 0.0001 and decays based on the inverse square root of the number of training steps.
keyInnovations: Multi-query attention for reduced memory usage while maintaining performance.
Curriculum learning to teach complex tasks progressively.
Dynamic learning rate adjustments to adapt to the model's learning phase.

experiments.analysis: Our model outperformed both baselines, demonstrating its superior ability to generate coherent and contextually relevant text.
The enhancements in in-context learning capabilities resulted in significantly better performance in few-shot tasks, illustrating the efficacy of our architecture and training strategy.

keyPapers: Vaswani et al. (2017) - 'Attention is All You Need'
Radford et al. (2019) - 'Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners'
relatedWork.ourDifference: While previous works laid the foundational architecture, our study introduces specific innovations in attention mechanisms and training strategies that directly influence generative performance.

keyPapers: Kaplan et al. (2020) - 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models'
relatedWork.ourDifference: We extend the understanding of scaling laws by showing how architectural refinements can lead to better adherence to these laws in practice, contrary to the traditional view that simply increasing parameters suffices.

futureWork: Investigating the effects of model pruning techniques on performance and efficiency.
Exploring the integration of multimodal inputs to enhance contextual understanding and generation.
Developing unsupervised fine-tuning methods to improve model adaptability across diverse tasks.
